notes: hold-down = fixed lip over the top front edge between the camera windows + rear cantilever latch; formulas in cad/holddown.py

retaining face raked 14.0 deg (nose lowest): the nose corner bears on the flat top of the marker, so the frictionless reaction is vertical and the face cannot cam the latch open while the hook turns nose-up under load; the retention figure is the frictionless lower bound and includes that rotation and the growth of the lever as the beam leans back
'governing position' = marker against the front nest wall, where the lead-in of the hook leaves it during insertion: the overlap is then 0.25 mm smaller than with the marker centred

insertion path: the marker is tilted nose-down, rests 0.05 mm above the front strip of the nest floor and is as far forward as the front nest wall, the nose pocket and the lip tip allow (0.05 mm clear); at each tilt the solids of tub + base plate + balls are intersected with the cradle (latch removed), the free-length plungers with base plate and adhesive sheet, and the latch is turned back until it no longer intersects the marker (that travel is the insertion deflection)

hook travel = backward travel of the beam axis at the nose level; because the hook also turns nose-up, the nose corner itself moves a little further, which is why the travel that frees the marker is smaller than the distance nose to marker edge

latch deflection in the posed checks = rigid rotation of the solid about the point that reproduces tip travel and tip slope of the bent beam (7.40 mm below the nose level for a tip force, 5.77 mm for a pure moment); exact for hook and tab

FE: plane strain, 82410 constant-strain triangles on the section x = 5.2 of the cradle solid, 0.025 mm elements at the fillets, nodal-averaged principal strain; skin under the well free and PCB-backed, the larger value is used (cad/latchfe.py). Refining the fillet mesh from 0.035 to 0.025 mm raised the root peak by 2 %

free plunger tip at z = 2.105; the pads meet the plungers at about 1.9 deg of tilt. The cradle PCB top is set 5.82 mm below the COPPER FACE of the pads (z 0.965), which is modelled 0.035 mm below the YAML pad plane (z 1.0)
printability of the latch is covered by check 5 (walls) and check 6 (the latch well is open at the top and drained; its gaps are listed there)

insertion 11 N and release 9 to 12 N are estimates (friction 0.3 assumed, modulus from the data sheet, dry PA12); pin force and stroke are PROVISIONAL
retention with the overlap reduced by 0.3 mm is 3.4 x at E = 1700 MPa and needs E >= 1485 MPa: the distance front nest wall to hook nose is a first-article dimension

deviations.requirement: every printed wall >= 0.8 mm
deviations.implemented: the wall behind each window recess in front of the camera cube is 0.525 mm: z 4.2..4.6 across the 4.0 mm bay (1.6 mm2 per camera); the bonded window backs it
deviations.reason: visor face 18.4 to cube front 17.075 leaves 1.325 mm for recess 0.55 + wall 0.8 + clearance 0.25. Accepted in rev C (visor_window.min_wall_behind_recess = 0.525)

deviations.requirement: camera opening bevelled wider toward the inside
deviations.implemented: no bevel: the opening is straight, +-2.0 wide and z 4.6..6.8, and as wide as the prism bay behind it (bay half-width 2.0); it runs from the floor of the window recess (y 17.85) straight into the bay, over a sill 0.525 mm thick
deviations.reason: the light bundle diverges outward: it is +-1.62 mm wide at the aperture plane (the recess floor) and +-1.37 mm at the inner edge of the sill, 0.525 mm further in, so a bevel toward the inside clears nothing. A wider bay would push the hood beyond the 2.85 mm half-width of the keep-out contract (hood outside is +-2.8)

deviations.requirement: shallow glue channel if possible without going below the wall minimum
deviations.implemented: no glue channel and no glue chamfer anywhere
deviations.reason: the arc ledge is 0.65 mm wide and the seal land 0.4 mm: any groove leaves a seal lip below 0.5 mm, and a chamfer on the 0.8 mm visor wall leaves less than 0.8 at its foot. The 0.25 mm radial groove between base edge and side wall is the adhesive reservoir on the arc (it is filled down to the rim and modelled as part of the bead); the joint on the land is 0.33 mm high

deviations.requirement: two or three 1.2 mm locating pins/keys between base and tub so that the base cannot be assembled rotated
deviations.implemented: no key between base plate and tub; the edge of the base plate is plain. The base plate is laminated to the PCB in a jig that locates the PCB by its two locating holes and the plate by its D outline; the PCB / base unit is then located in the tub by the two spigots of posts E
deviations.reason: there is no room for a key inside the seal line, and a key under the visor wall interrupts the seal land: the two lugs of the first rev C model sat in through-notches that connected the underside to the camera bays (design review; check 13 now proves the seal ring is closed). A key with 0.25 mm clearance could not hold the 0.249 mm between baffle ring and photodiode either

deviations.requirement: vent pad near (17, -3) (rev B)
deviations.reason: rev C YAML gives this position

deviations.requirement: nose groove from the aperture edge to the visor
deviations.implemented: groove 1.0 x 0.3 from the cover-glass recess edge (r 14.25) to the visor; roof thickened 0.3 mm underneath
deviations.reason: the aperture edge is under the cover glass; the thickening keeps 0.8 mm under the groove

deviations.requirement: adhesive sheet at zero thickness in the YAML (rev B)
deviations.implemented: base plate 0.87 + sheet 0.13 (z 0.87..1.0); PCB at z 1.0..1.8; no modelling overlap
deviations.reason: rev C YAML: base_plate.thickness 0.87 and base_plate.psa.thickness 0.13

deviations.requirement: LCD glass assembled from below
deviations.implemented: the glass is tilted in: rear edge first at 6 deg, shifted 0.55 mm toward the visor while its rear corners pass the seating ledge, then pushed back and hinged up (assembly step, path proven in check 14)
deviations.reason: rear glass corners are at r = 21.427 > ledge inner radius 21.35. Rev C accepted a flat insertion biased 0.25 mm forward (0.118 mm to the ledge, less than the print tolerance); the design review showed that the flat glass cannot go further forward because posts E stop it. Tilted, the front edge is still below the post feet while the rear corners pass, so the shift can be 0.55 mm (corners at r = 20.999)

deviations.requirement: 0.25 mm clearance on every drop-in fit
deviations.implemented: PCB edge to seating ledge 0.25 mm; visor window in its recess 0.25 mm per side
deviations.reason: rev C YAML: pcb.radius 21.1 and visor_window.recess_w 5.5

deviations.requirement: light baffle from the visor wall back to each prism (light-tight)
deviations.implemented: hood: side skirts and a front pad down to z 3.0, rear wall down to z 4.81 (over the cube); bottom front edge of the rear wall chamfered 0.12 mm (0.26 mm to the prism hypotenuse). A slit of 0.25 to 0.37 mm remains above the cube at the rear; it is closed by a bead of black adhesive (0.25 mm wide, dispensed 0.6 mm high on the underside of the rear wall and CURED before the PCB is joined, so that the cube top beds into a soft gasket)
deviations.reason: the rear wall cannot pass the cube (LCD glass 0.63 mm behind it). Rev C: the slit is closed with black adhesive at assembly. A bead applied wet and closed blind (first rev C sequence) would squeeze out next to the prism and glue the PCB to the tub before any test (design review), hence the pre-cured bead; the gaps beside and in front of the cube (0.265 / 0.25 mm) stay open: light-leak test

deviations.requirement: top edge radius 0.6, bottom chamfer 0.3; cavity below z 1.2 = R 22 circle clipped at the visor face
deviations.implemented: radius and chamfer on the arc only (visor edges sharp); below z = 1.2 the side wall ends on the radial plane through the outer D corner (+-13.8, 18.4), which leaves an open pocket about 2.0 mm wide under each end of the visor wall. The pockets lie OUTSIDE the seal ring (the bead runs round both D corners on the base land)
deviations.reason: the windows are flush with the top, a rounded visor edge would leave them proud; the R 22 circle meets the visor plane at 33 deg and would leave feather-edged wall ends; the radial cut keeps the full 1.0 mm wall at the end face

deviations.requirement: nest accepts the puck at 0 and 180 deg (rev B)
deviations.implemented: one orientation only; the D flat is the key
deviations.reason: rev C: the cradle is a charging and data dock; calibration does not use it

deviations.requirement: seven 2.0 mm pin holes and a stainless reference plate (rev B)
deviations.implemented: one printed slot 2.33 mm wide through the nest floor; no plate
deviations.reason: rev C: 'spring pins come up through one slot'; the reference plate is deleted

deviations.requirement: hold the marker down against the spring pins (open in rev B)
deviations.implemented: fixed lip (|x| <= 6.0, 1.2 mm over the tub top) and a rear cantilever latch (24.0 wide, 1.05 / 0.85 / 1.3 thick, 11.65 mm long, nose 0.85 to 1.10 mm on the tub top) with a thumb tab and two over-travel stops
deviations.reason: designed and proven in check 7 (retention with tolerance, strain by formula and FE, forces, posed insertion and release)

deviations.requirement: four 3 mm feet pockets; PCB pocket underneath
deviations.implemented: four pockets dia 8.4 x 1.0 for dia 8.0 x 3.0 mm adhesive bumpers, each with a blind core dia 5.0 behind it (the corners would otherwise be 13 mm solid); PCB held against the pocket ceiling by four M2 thread-forming screws (not modelled; printed as dia 1.7 x 0.5 spot marks, drilled dia 1.6 x 3 after printing because a blind 1.7 mm hole would trap powder); three lightening pockets underneath
deviations.reason: '3 mm feet' read as 3 mm high bumpers (ambiguous); the pin force pushes the PCB out of its pocket so it needs positive retention

deviations.requirement: PCB located to the tub by two printed spigots in non-plated holes (rev C YAML)
deviations.implemented: spigots dia 1.0 x 0.6 under posts E (tip chamfered 0.15 as a lead-in) in a dia 1.15 hole and a 1.15 x 1.65 slot: 0.075 mm radial clearance, as specified
deviations.reason: 0.075 mm is a locating fit, far below the 0.25 mm drop-in rule and below the +-0.2 mm print tolerance: a spigot that prints 0.15 mm oversize does not enter. The spigots are therefore a gauged feature (go / no-go at first article, dress with a hollow punch or fine file). They are 8.4 mm apart while the cameras are 20 mm apart, so their play is amplified at the cameras, and they only locate until the adhesives have cured (a dia 1.0 PA12 pin cannot hold the board against the base laminate). PROPOSED_PARAM_CHANGES.md proposes to move the pair to posts B

deviations.requirement: cradle body 60 x 60 x 14 mm
deviations.implemented: body 60 x 60 x 14 (z -11.0 to 3.0); the lip stands to z 9.45 and the latch to z 11.63, so the printed part is 22.6 mm tall; the body is not centred on the marker (y -36.0 to 24.0)
deviations.reason: a hook over the marker top (z 7.6) with a 11.65 mm cantilever and a 30 deg lead-in cannot stay inside a 14 mm block; the rear needs the room for the latch well, the guard wall, the tab stop and the USB-C receptacle

deviations.requirement: the marker rests on its three ball feet on the nest floor, pins at the working height
deviations.implemented: lip and hook have the 0.25 mm drop-in clearance above the tub top. With pins fitted the marker is pushed up against them: it floats up to 0.25 mm above its feet and the pins then stand 6.07 instead of 5.82 mm high (0.89 of 2.29 mm stroke used)
deviations.reason: a retaining face with drop-in clearance cannot preload a part whose height varies by the print tolerance; the float is inside the pin stroke. A dock does not need a seating datum (calibration is done elsewhere)

deviations.requirement: tub_keepouts is the complete contract: every tub feature that touches or hangs over the PCB top lies inside it
deviations.implemented: true for everything below z = 4.35 (2.55 mm above the PCB top), which check 12 proves on the solids. Above that height the tub still has features over the PCB outside the keep-outs: glass locating ribs down to z 4.75, the thick roof at z 5.55 (also behind and beside the LCD glass), the nose pad at z 6.5 and the vent pad at z 6.5
deviations.reason: design/check_layout.py lets a part outside the LCD footprint reach z = roof - 0.1 = 6.7. No listed part is taller than 2.0 mm there, so nothing clashes today, but the rule and the tub disagree: a free height must be added to the contract

deviations.requirement: tub side wall from z = 0 (the base plane) to the top
deviations.implemented: the side wall ends 0.25 mm above the base plane (rim relief): the tub is 7.35 mm tall, the marker still 7.6 mm. The rim is 0.35 mm above the plane of the ball feet
deviations.reason: with rim and base plate in one plane the feet stood only 0.1 mm proud of a rim whose height is set by a four-part stack (post, PCB, sheet, plate: +-0.16 mm RSS, +-0.29 worst case): about one unit in ten would have rocked on its rim (design review). Price: on a hard floor the side wall no longer shares a footstep load until the base has given by the relief (open issue)

deviations.requirement: vent on a pad raised 0.2 mm (YAML vent.location); plain top face
deviations.implemented: pad raised 0.3 mm and run out to the side wall; two grooves 0.6 wide x 0.3 deep through the vent hole on the top face, one of them over the edge radius (drain), the other +-2.5 mm across
deviations.reason: the vent hole is a well on the face that is stepped on: it ponds water and a shoe sole can seal it and pump the membrane (design review). The grooves let it drain and breathe; 0.8 mm of roof stays under them thanks to the thicker pad

deviations.requirement: the marker rests on its three ball feet on the printed nest floor
deviations.implemented: the feet rest on a front strip (y >= 12.8) and two round pads dia 4.0 at the level z = -0.1; the rest of the floor is a basin 0.65 mm lower on the centre line that falls 2.0 deg to both sides and out through the finger scallops. A rim 1.2 mm wide round the pin slot and a dam in front of the latch well stay at strip level; the latch well drains through a 2.4 x 2.4 mm tunnel to the rear face
deviations.reason: a flat floor 0.10 mm under the marker held a film of water whose only drain was the pin slot, straight onto the cradle PCB, and the latch well was a blind sump above that PCB (design review: wet docking)

deviations.requirement: adhesive frame bonding the LCD under the roof ledge (closed frame)
deviations.implemented: frame with a 0.8 mm vent channel from the dia 23.0 window to its rear right corner (in the die-cut GL1-030)
deviations.reason: a closed frame makes the 450 mm3 between cover glass and LCD a sealed cell that the vent does not serve: +16 kPa at 70 C on both bond lines, and fogging (design review). The channel is 0.15 mm high and hidden under the roof ledge

deviations.requirement: ball top 0.03 above the plate inside a 2.0 mm hole of the adhesive sheet (YAML comment); potting from the inside before the sheet
deviations.implemented: as specified, plus a second stage: at lamination the three sheet holes are filled with the potting epoxy, so that each ball bears on the PCB underside through 0.10 mm of epoxy in compression (stage 1 dome at most 0.08 mm)
deviations.reason: in straight through holes the balls are held only by the shear strength of the potting (about 3 mm2 of hole wall): a step on a hard floor pushes them in (design review). The backing needs the PCB underside to be free of tracks and vias under the feet (proposal)

deviations.requirement: cradle pins at their working height on the pad plane z = 1.0
deviations.implemented: cradle PCB top at z = -4.855: the pins stand 5.82 mm on the COPPER FACE of the pads, which is modelled 0.035 mm below the board underside (z 0.965)
deviations.reason: the first rev C model put the board 5.82 below the board underside, so the modelled pins stood 5.785 mm while every table said 5.82 (design review). pad_plane_z should say which face it means
